name: Wait. What Is That? (Case File 00, free)
when: DEFAULT plug for casual interest: someone enjoying the cases, asking if there are more, or new to the account. A free 2-minute guessing game on the phone with 6 X-rays of things that should not be inside a person (a coin, a spoon, a razor blade, a nail in an eye socket, a metal rod and a tooth in the chest). Each reveal says what it is and what happens next. No app and no sign up.

name: How Did That Get In There? (Case File 01)
when: Cheap or impulse asks ('is there a cheaper one') and swallowed-object or foreign-body comments ('how did that get in there'). A phone game with 10 X-rays of things found inside people, among them a fork, a safety pin, a sword, a battery in a nose and scissors left behind after surgery. Each reveal says how it got there and whether it can be fixed. Solo or party mode for 2 to 6 players on one phone.

name: What Am I Even Looking At? (Case File 02)
when: Someone asking 'is there a book', wanting the cases explained, or asking whether these can be fixed. 10 of the weirdest X-rays as a PDF book with a guess page and an answer page for each (what it is, why it happens and whether it can be fixed in plain words) plus the same 10 as a scored phone game.

name: I Could Read These All Day (Case File 03)
when: Superfans: 'I could read these all day', 'I'd buy all of them', asks for everything in one place. Every case file in one library: both games, the book, the archive of posted cases and every new file from here on at no extra cost. Never state a case count for it.

name: Keep The Cases Coming
when: Someone who wants to support the account or the creator ('how can I support you', 'you deserve to be paid for this', 'take my money'). A pay-what-you-want way to help keep the nightly cases free for everyone. It has no cases in it.

name: It's Just Anxiety — the medical gaslighting card game
when: Jokes or stories about being dismissed by doctors ('they said it was anxiety/stress/in my head') where the commenter is JOKING, not sharing raw pain — 120 cards, most dismissive answer wins.
